title: JRC EV Cold Weather Real-World Energy Consumption & Sub-Zero Range Degradation
metadata_text:
Title: JRC EV Cold Weather Real-World Energy Consumption & Sub-Zero Range Degradation
Organization: European Commission - Joint Research Centre (JRC)
Source URL: https://data.jrc.ec.europa.eu/dataset/jrc-bev-cold-temp-2024
Category: electric_vehicle
Publication Year: 2024
Tags: electric vehicle, cold weather, range degradation, BEV, battery efficiency, VELA

Description:
Comprehensive empirical dataset recorded by the European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC) Vehicle Emissions Laboratory (VELA 2). Analyzes battery electric vehicle (BEV) performance at ambient temperatures from -15°C to 23°C across WLTC and real-world urban/highway drive cycles. Key findings demonstrate a 28% to 42% range reduction at sub-zero temperatures due to lithium-ion electrochemical impedance increase and 3.8 kW HVAC resistive cabin heating. Grid pre-conditioning mitigates thermal energy penalty by 18%.

Available Resources:
- JRC_EV_Cold_Weather_Report_2024.pdf (PDF): Technical report on sub-zero BEV energy consumption and thermal cabin HVAC power draw.

title: JRC VELA Laboratory: BEV Heat Pump Coefficient of Performance (COP) & Range Recovery Analysis
metadata_text:
Title: JRC VELA Laboratory: BEV Heat Pump Coefficient of Performance (COP) & Range Recovery Analysis
Organization: European Commission - Joint Research Centre (JRC)
Source URL: https://data.jrc.ec.europa.eu/dataset/jrc-bev-heat-pump-cop-2024
Category: electric_vehicle
Publication Year: 2024
Tags: electric vehicle, heat pump, COP, thermal management, PTC heater, BEV efficiency

Description:
Comparative assessment of BEV thermal management architectures featuring R744 (CO2) and R1234yf heat pumps versus positive temperature coefficient (PTC) resistive heaters. Heat pump thermal circuits maintained an average COP of 2.1 at -5°C ambient, reducing cabin heating power draw from 3.5 kW to 1.2 kW and preserving 15-22% total vehicle range.

Available Resources:
- JRC_Heat_Pump_BEV_Efficiency_2024.pdf (PDF): Heat pump COP measurements and cabin thermal comfort evaluations in VELA climate chambers.

title: JRC Battery Cell Durability: High-Power Fast Charging (DCFC) Thermal Stress & Capacity Fade
metadata_text:
Title: JRC Battery Cell Durability: High-Power Fast Charging (DCFC) Thermal Stress & Capacity Fade
Organization: European Commission - Joint Research Centre (JRC)
Source URL: https://data.jrc.ec.europa.eu/dataset/jrc-bev-fast-charge-degradation-2023
Category: electric_vehicle
Publication Year: 2023
Tags: electric vehicle, fast charging, battery degradation, NMC, LFP, SEI layer

Description:
Accelerated aging study of NMC-811 and LFP battery cells under 150 kW - 350 kW DC Fast Charging regimes. Demonstrates solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) growth acceleration when fast-charging below 15°C cell core temperature without pre-heating, causing 12% faster capacity fade over 800 cycles.

Available Resources:
- JRC_DCFC_Battery_Aging_Study_2023.pdf (PDF): Experimental battery degradation profiles under ultra-fast DC charging profiles.

Category: electric_vehicle
Publication Year: 2023
Tags: electric vehicle, State of Health, SoH, battery durability, BMS, Euro 7

Description:
Validation of onboard battery management system (BMS) SoH accuracy across 450 field electric vehicles. Findings indicate BMS SoH algorithms overestimate remaining capacity by 2.4% after 5 years, supporting EU Euro 7 battery durability regulatory standards (80% capacity retention after 5 yrs / 100,000 km).

title: JRC Market Surveillance: Real-World Fuel Consumption vs official WLTP Ratings for Plug-In Hybrids
metadata_text:
Title: JRC Market Surveillance: Real-World Fuel Consumption vs official WLTP Ratings for Plug-In Hybrids
Organization: European Commission - Joint Research Centre (JRC)
Source URL: https://data.jrc.ec.europa.eu/dataset/jrc-phev-wltp-gap-2023
Category: phev_hybrids
Publication Year: 2023
Tags: plug-in hybrid, PHEV, WLTP gap, real world fuel consumption, OBFCM, utility factor

Description:
Evaluation of On-Board Fuel Consumption Monitoring (OBFCM) data collected from 123,000 Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEVs) across Europe. Real-world fuel consumption averages 3.5 to 4.2 times higher (4.0-4.5 l/100km higher) than official WLTP homologation values (1.2-1.5 l/100km). Discrepancy is caused by lower real-world utility factors (infrequent charging) and engine starts during high thermal heating demand.

Available Resources:
- JRC_PHEV_OBFCM_Monitoring_2023.pdf (PDF): Analysis of real-world PHEV fuel consumption and utility factor deviations in Europe.

Description:
